class_name: 不許可-不許可-テハイケナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: The everyday prohibition: doing the named thing is not allowed, either as a standing rule (試験中は辞書を使ってはいけません) or as a stop-that aimed at the person in front of you (無理しちゃいけない). てはならない is the institutional sibling and ちゃだめ the casual spoken one. It typically comes from someone entitled to prohibit, so aimed upward use ご遠慮ください or 〜ないでください instead.

examples.ruby: 試験中[しけんちゅう]は辞書[じしょ]を使[つか]ってはいけません。
examples.english: You may not use a dictionary during the exam.

examples.ruby: まだ熱[ねつ]があるから、無理[むり]しちゃいけないよ。
examples.english: You've still got a fever, so you mustn't push yourself.

examples.ruby: 人[ひと]の手紙[てがみ]を勝手[かって]に読[よ]んじゃいけない。
examples.english: You don't get to read other people's letters without asking.

patterns.usage_note: Prohibition stated as a rule binding everyone rather than a scolding of the person present: 図書館の本に線を引いてはならない, 教訓を忘れてはならない. てはいけない is the everyday sibling and ちゃだめ the casual one. It is far more common in writing, regulations and speeches than in conversation, and the frequent なくてはならない is the obligation form, not this prohibition.

examples.ruby: 図書館[としょかん]の本[ほん]に、線[せん]を引[ひ]いてはならない。
examples.english: You are not to underline anything in a library book.

examples.ruby: プールでは、走[はし]ったり飛[と]び込[こ]んだりしてはなりません。
examples.english: Running and diving are not permitted at the pool.

examples.ruby: 我々[われわれ]はこの事故[じこ]の教訓[きょうくん]を忘[わす]れてはならない。
examples.english: We must never forget the lesson of this accident.

patterns.usage_note: The casual spoken prohibition, literally "doing it is no good": 大声を出しちゃだめだよ, said to the person you are talking to and often softened with よ or って. てはいけない covers the same ground in neutral and written registers, てはならない in regulations; ちゃだめ stays out of both. It also takes a たら conditional (飲んだらだめ) alongside the て-form.

examples.ruby: 子供[こども]がいるんだから、そんな大声[おおごえ]を出[だ]しちゃだめだよ。
examples.english: There are kids around, so don't go shouting like that.

examples.ruby: そっちを見[み]ちゃだめ、まだ準備中[じゅんびちゅう]だから。
examples.english: Don't look over there, we're still getting it ready.

examples.ruby: 薬[くすり]をお酒[さけ]と一緒[いっしょ]に飲[の]んじゃだめだよ。
examples.english: You really shouldn't take your medicine with alcohol.

patterns.usage_note: The prohibition of signs, notices, house rules and proverbs: it closes the sentence with no copula (立入るべからず), and the adnominal べからざる modifies a following noun (許すべからざる行為). It is the classical ancestor of てはいけない, not a variant of it, and it is not used in ordinary conversation. With する the classical stem gives すべからず, though するべからず also occurs.

examples.ruby: 危険[きけん]につき、この先[さき]へ立入[たちい]るべからず。
examples.english: Danger: no entry beyond this point.

examples.ruby: 社外[しゃがい]の者[もの]に本資料[ほんしりょう]を見[み]せるべからず。
examples.english: This document is not to be shown to anyone outside the company.

examples.ruby: それは仲間[なかま]として許[ゆる]すべからざる裏切[うらぎ]りだった。
examples.english: It was a betrayal no comrade could ever forgive.
